_comment: Machine-readable index of all transaction XDR fixtures. Consumers must pass the recorded passphrase to TransactionBuilder.fromXDR — the XDR encoding does not embed the network passphrase and decoding under a wrong passphrase will succeed silently but produce a wrong transaction hash.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: Sends XLM to suspicious_wallet_1, a pass-through wallet. No funds are lost to a known attacker, but the destination is a likely laundering hop.
fixtures.description: Plain payment from clean_wallet_1 to suspicious_wallet_1. Tests basic payment decode.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: Delivers funds to malicious_wallet_1, a sweep wallet that drains deposits within seconds.
fixtures.description: Path payment strict-send (XLM → USDC) from clean_wallet_1 to malicious_wallet_1. Tests multi-hop decode.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: Opens a trustline to the SCAM rug-pull asset. A trustline alone moves no funds, so the transaction is suspicious rather than malicious; it is the first step of a rug-pull purchase.
fixtures.description: Change trust to add the SCAM asset trustline from suspicious_wallet_1. Tests trustline-establishment decode.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: Same inner payment as payment.xdr (to a pass-through wallet), wrapped in a fee bump paid by clean_wallet_2. The fee source is clean, so the label follows the inner payment.
fixtures.description: Fee-bump wrapping payment.xdr. Outer fee source is clean_wallet_2; inner tx source is clean_wallet_1. Tests fee-bump envelope decode — a decoder must traverse into the inner transaction to extract operations and source; reading the top-level source gives the fee-bump source, not the transaction initiator.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: Both parties are ordinary clean wallets; nothing about the operation is risky.
fixtures.description: Plain XLM payment between two clean wallets.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: Pays a clean merchant in a clean, widely held asset.
fixtures.description: TUSD payment to a merchant.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: Depositing to an exchange hot wallet with a memo id is the normal custodial deposit flow.
fixtures.description: Exchange deposit with a memo-id routing tag.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The recipient and the asset are clean, and the path crosses only the clean distributor's offer.
fixtures.description: Path payment strict-send XLM -> TUSD to a clean wallet, filled against the clean TUSD market.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The recipient and the asset are clean.
fixtures.description: Path payment strict-receive XLM -> 20 TUSD to a merchant.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: A fee bump only changes who pays the fee. The fee source and recipient are both clean.
fixtures.description: Fee-bump envelope: clean-relayer pays the fee for a clean XLM payment.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: TUSD is a clean, widely held asset.
fixtures.description: changeTrust to the clean TUSD asset.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The claimant already trusts TUSD, and the balance comes from a clean distributor.
fixtures.description: Claim a TUSD claimable balance created by the clean distributor.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: A token transfer via the clean TUSD contract to a clean wallet.
fixtures.description: Soroban invokeHostFunction: TUSD SAC transfer(from, to, 10 TUSD) between clean wallets.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The allowance is small and short-lived, and the spender is a clean dApp. It has the same shape as an approval drain, which makes it a false-positive probe.
fixtures.description: Soroban approve(): 10 TUSD allowance to a known dApp spender, expiring in ~720 ledgers (~1h).

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The owner keeps its master key (weight 1) and needs both keys for payments. That adds security rather than handing over control. Same operation type as a signer takeover, so it is a false-positive probe.
fixtures.description: setOptions: add clean-cosigner (weight 1) and raise med/high thresholds to 2, making a 2-of-2 multisig.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The merge destination belongs to the same synthetic user. Same operation as a merge drain, so it is a false-positive probe.
fixtures.description: accountMerge: clean-closer closes its account into the same user's clean-savings.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: Every recipient is clean. The high fan-out resembles a pass-through distribution, which makes it a false-positive probe.
fixtures.description: Five-operation payroll batch paying 40 XLM to five clean wallets.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: An ordinary DEX trade into a clean asset.
fixtures.description: manageSellOffer selling 20 XLM for TUSD at 1.9 TUSD/XLM, crossing the clean market.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The recipient is clean but has no history (the clean counterpart of a cold-start scam).
fixtures.description: XLM payment to a freshly funded clean wallet with no history.

fixtures.label: clean
fixtures.rationale: The recipient is clean. The fixture exists to catch tiering off-by-one errors.
fixtures.description: XLM payment to clean-boundary, whose stub score is exactly 20 (low/elevated boundary).

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: The recipient is a laundering hop rather than the final beneficiary.
fixtures.description: XLM payment to pass-through-1, which forwards it to sweeper-1 within the minute (see evidence).

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: The recipient is a laundering hop. The path itself crosses only the clean market.
fixtures.description: Path payment strict-send XLM -> TUSD to pass-through-2, which forwards TUSD to sweeper-2.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: The recipient is a laundering hop. The fixture exists to catch tiering off-by-one errors.
fixtures.description: XLM payment to pass-through-boundary (stub score 51: elevated/high boundary).

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: The recipient impersonates a support desk via memos. The loss is a small fee, so suspicious rather than malicious.
fixtures.description: Pays 25 XLM "KYC verification fee" to memo-impersonator-1 after receiving its refund-lure memo.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: The issuer can claw back the balance (executed on-chain in the follow-up evidence). The user should be told, but this is not theft.
fixtures.description: changeTrust to CLAW, an asset whose issuer has AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: The new account depends on an attacker-controlled sponsor (mule infrastructure). Signed by both parties.
fixtures.description: begin/endSponsoringFutureReserves + createAccount: malicious-sponsor creates sponsored-mule-1 with sponsored reserves.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: A trustline alone moves no funds, so this is suspicious rather than malicious. It is the first step of buying a rug-pull token (see malicious_path_buy_rug_token).
fixtures.description: changeTrust to RUGX, the rug-pull token.

fixtures.label: suspicious
fixtures.rationale: Claiming spam engages the user with the attacker's asset (a phishing lure), but no funds leave the account.
fixtures.description: Multi-op: changeTrust AIRDROP + claimClaimableBalance of an unsolicited airdrop.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: The funds land with a final collection wallet for stolen funds.
fixtures.description: Path payment strict-send XLM -> TUSD delivered to sweeper-1.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: The inner payment drains the victim to a phishing drainer, and the outer fee source is also attacker-controlled. A decoder must look inside the fee bump.
fixtures.description: Fee-bump: phishing-drainer-2 pays the fee for a 5,000 XLM payment from victim-4 to phishing-drainer-1 ("gasless" lure).

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: The victim permanently hands sole control to the attacker. The follow-up evidence shows the attacker draining the account.
fixtures.description: setOptions: add takeover-attacker-1 as signer (weight 255) and set master weight to 0.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: The attacker key alone can now authorise any operation, including payments and merges.
fixtures.description: setOptions: add takeover-attacker-2 (weight 1) and set all thresholds to 1.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: Transfers the entire balance to an attacker and deletes the victim account. This cannot be undone.
fixtures.description: accountMerge: victim-merge-1 merges its whole account into merge-drainer-1.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: A token transfer to a malicious collection wallet via a clean contract. The contract is clean; the recipient argument is not.
fixtures.description: Soroban TUSD SAC transfer(victim-5, sweeper-2, 100 TUSD).

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: An unlimited, months-long allowance to an unknown spender. The spender then calls transfer_from and drains the balance (evidence).
fixtures.description: Soroban TUSD SAC approve(victim-5, approval-drainer-1, i128::MAX, +1,000,000 ledgers).

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: A large, long-lived XLM allowance to an unknown spender, which is then drained via transfer_from (evidence).
fixtures.description: Soroban native XLM SAC approve(victim-6, approval-drainer-2, 9,000 XLM, +1,000,000 ledgers).

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: An innocuous-looking first operation hides a payment to a sweeper and a signer takeover. The label follows the worst operation.
fixtures.description: Three-op bundle: changeTrust RUGX + 500 XLM payment to sweeper-3 + setOptions adding takeover-attacker-3 (weight 10).

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: A small legitimate-looking payment precedes a full-account drain.
fixtures.description: Two-op bundle: 1 XLM to a clean merchant, then accountMerge into merge-drainer-2.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: The recipient is a scam collection wallet by construction. Its low stub score models the oracle's cold-start blind spot, so this fixture is an expected miss for the reputation-only path.
fixtures.description: 750 XLM payment to cold-start-scam-1, a freshly funded scam wallet with no history.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: Converts real value into a token whose entire supply is controlled and dumped by the issuer.
fixtures.description: Path payment strict-receive: spend up to 200 XLM to buy 1,000 RUGX from the rug issuer's offer.

fixtures.label: malicious
fixtures.rationale: A large payment to a known phishing drainer.
fixtures.description: 2,500 XLM payment from victim-8 to phishing-drainer-2, which had dusted it with a "test" payment.
